newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to study further insurance liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to study further insurance liberalisation.

text.p: Sri Lanka plans to launch a study looking further liberalisation of its insurance sector next year, Mano Tittawela, director general of Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC) said on Tuesday.
"We want to kick off a study in 1998 to look at government holdings in non-commercial areas of financial services, including the insurance industry," Tittawell said.

He said PERC will commission a study in 1998 on liberalising the insurance sector and divesting government minority and majority holdings in areas of financial services such as development finance, housing, leasing, venture capital and asset management.
Sri Lanka has two state-owned insurance firms -- Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation and the National Insurance Corporation and three private insurance companies.
